BiblicalUsage: Chanukkah is the dedication of the altar and the house, and it always comes with offerings. The princes offered at the dedication of the altar, and this was the dedication after the altar was anointed. Solomon kept the dedication of the altar seven days and the feast seven days, and at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem the Levites were sought out to keep it with gladness and thanksgiving.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe dedication in Scripture is never a ribbon-cutting but a giving: the altar is dedicated by what is laid on it, and the wall by the songs sung over it. I hold that God receives a house the way He receives a sacrifice, by what His people bring to it.
